scope: phase_B_foundation; supplied full current source/tests and explicitly labeled integration diff if present

findings.title: Revoke-then-replace resurrects a revoked grant as active
findings.issue: revoke_grant only increments the stored revision and writes revoked_at in the document; replace_grant then accepts any grant with revision<grant.revision and rewrites the document without carrying revoked_at forward. After revocation, a stale in-memory grant with a higher revision is re-registered as 'active', so an authorization that must be denied becomes allowed.
findings.fix: Persist revocation as an irreversible terminal state (e.g. revoked flag/column checked before any replacement) or reject replacement once revoked_at is set; add a test that revoke followed by replace_grant keeps the grant non-authorizable.

findings.title: Persisted ActionConfirmation lacks expiry binding and validation
findings.issue: _confirmation blindly reconstructs ActionConfirmation from stored JSON without validating digest/actor/expires_at bounds or matching the persisted confirmation against the proposal timestamp. Combined with confirm()'s idempotency-key reuse (an existing unconsumed row is returned even if its payload belongs to an older/different proposal state), a confirmation replayed after the intended one-use binding has changed can still satisfy action.consume(now) because expiry is taken solely from attacker-influenced stored fields.
findings.fix: Validate confirmation expiry and payload integrity on load, bind the stored confirmation to the exact proposal digest/version at insert, and refuse reuse of an idempotency key whose confirmation was produced for a different proposal state; add regression tests.

findings.title: Two-phase compound reservation allows an allow to proceed after a scope-group denial
findings.issue: execute_reserved_groups commits each group to 'prepared' before the final authorization pass; if the second group is denied at the final check, the first group is settled 'unknown' but the exception is re-raised as ScopeTransportUnknown only when transport_started is true, otherwise as ScopePreparationUnknown. The caller sees a non-retryable error but the durable 'prepared' fence leaves windows reserved and call-counts incremented while no transport ran, effectively consuming budget for an operation that never occurred and preventing normal reconciliation.
findings.fix: Distinguish pre-transport denials (rollback/abandon all prepared groups and refund reservations) from post-transport unknowns; only mark 'prepared'/charge call-counts immediately before the actual I/O point or provide an explicit reconciliation path for the untouched case.

not_verified: the public integration diff (phase D) and any unchanged legacy modules
production/live data paths and real external providers
findings.summary: Most durability, fencing, and fail-closed paths are solid and well-tested, but three P1 defects undermine core safety invariants: revocation is not irreversible under grant replacement, confirmation persistence/replay validation is incomplete, and compound scope preparation can consume durable budget without any transport having occurred when a later scope is denied. These should be fixed before SHIP_OK; no P0 was found.
